utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. The witness should be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Your Honours, good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just wanted to let you know that the 65 ter 7604, which is the document I was using last with the witness yesterday, has been uploaded, the first page that was missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Skrbic. Welcome back to the courtroom. If there is any need to have a break, please let me know immediately. I have to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth still applies today. Mr. Vanderpuye is continuing his cross-examination. You have the floor, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And good morning to you, Your Honours, and everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Skrbic. Before we pick up where we --

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- left off yesterday, I just wanted to ask you a couple of other questions. From your CV it's not very clear - or from your testimony - but have you actually testified as an expert or prepared an expert report in any other proceeding besides this one?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. So this is your first time; yes?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put another question in relation to the CV, because you raised it. Mr. Skrbic, I would like to know what kind of additional education you went through besides your military career and education.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any additional education apart from military education.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What about statistic, mathematics? You spoke about mathematics and the importance of numbers. What did you learn about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I studied that at the military academy. We had mathematics 1 and mathematics 2, as well as in high school. So if you combine these two knowledges together, I am quite familiar with that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I was looking for any kind of list of publications attached to your reports. What kind of publications can we think of? Did you publish anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I published only one paper in the proceedings for the Russian Academy of Science, and my scientific work was entitled: "The Analysis of the Srebrenica Population." That was a paper delivered at an international conference held in Moscow in April 2009.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just follow-up on what the president is asking you. It is correct that you don't have an advanced degree or formal training in demography; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Or population statistics, statistics, mathematical demography, or sociology; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it's the case that your expert report on the population of Srebrenica actually didn't require any advanced degree or special training in any of those subjects; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. The calculations were very simple because I had at my disposal finalised facts and information, and anyone who know the basics of mathematics would be able to do that, provided they invest some effort into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I had asked, if I could, please, to have 65 ter 7604 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This was the letter that I showed you yesterday from the minister of defence of the Netherlands, dated October 20th, 1995. I just wanted to have it in the record so you could see that it's the same document I showed you yesterday; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it is -- I just want to confirm that this is the letter that you had not seen prior to yesterday; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And so you didn't see this document when you prepared your report. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would kindly ask the Registrar if that is -- if this document is identical with D314.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, 65 ter 7604, apart from this first page, contains additional two documents admitted as D314 and D315.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we please see D314 on the screen again. Mr. Skrbic, you see on the screen a document we have seen already yesterday. It's both in English at the moment. Did you use this document while you were preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't use this document. But I'd used another document that I showed to you, which is a diagram in which in the debriefing it says "flight from Srebrenica." I used also information from the article "The Icon of Srebrenica" from the journal the "Defence and Military Affairs," which states that there were 36 to 632 [as interpreted] refugees. I'm glad that you have showed me this document again and for giving me an opportunity to explain what the term "approximately" means in mathematics. Despite the fact that Mr. Prosecutor says that probably I don't have sufficient mathematical expertise, but I would like to remind you that yesterday afternoon I really made an effort in trying to remember which specific area of mathematics contains finding solutions for problems that are finally expressed not with an equation marks, which would be accuracy, but instead of the upper straight line in the equation mark you have a sinusoid line, whereas the lower line is straight; which, in mathematic terms, means either equal or approximate. That means that once you arrived at such a result after an analysis is nearly accurate or accurate. Thank you. And I really wanted to go back to this document in order to explain this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now see D315. Mr. Gajic, you have mentioned these two documents. I can't remember, at the moment, through which witness this was tendered by the Defence. Can you help me with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to the best of my recollection that was Mrs. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you have heard the motion of Mr. Vanderpuye by which he tendered the letter. We have seen from the minister of defence of the 20th of October, 1995. Do you have any objection?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Peace be upon this house. And my desire is that the outcome of this trial be decided by providence and God's will and not according to my wishes. Mr. President, I have no objection to any document that is going to speak about facts and information. I only think that we should admit into evidence documents in their entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, we have discussed this. The Chamber is not in a position to admit this document. By majority, the Presiding Judge dissenting. The reason is this witness has never seen this letter to Mr. Goldstone before, and therefore he can't testify about its content. That is --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- the position of the majority, Judge Fluegge dissenting.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Just to clarify on what the Presiding Judge has said: We are not saying you cannot tender this document in evidence; we are simply saying this is the wrong witness through which it's being tendered, since --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: -- there is no link between this document and this witness. As he says, he doesn't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Perhaps I can -- I can elucidate my position, if that would be of assistance to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yesterday I asked this witness specifically about this document in relation to the number 35.632 which was included in his report, and I asked him whether that was an accurate number or an estimate, as you will recall. And in response to that, he said that he believed that it was an accurate assessment because he based his report, in part, upon the debriefing information that he did review in preparing his report. The letter -- the cover letter of this document specifically speaks to the debriefing which this witness relied on in compiling his documents. And it says, very specifically: "I send a -- Herewith I send a document that was received during the debriefing of DutchBat about the registration of approximately 35.632 refugees." It is this document that is the basis of the information in the debriefing report that this witness relied upon. That's why I asked him if he'd seen this letter, because he's taken the debriefing report to be accurate, whereas this letter contradicts that. That's the basis of -- of admitting it in this case, because it shows that he did not review this letter which speaks to the reliability and the accuracy of the number that he ultimately relied on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Mindua has a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Good morning, Mr. Skrbic. I would like to verify something. In this letter sent by the defence minister of Holland, of the Dutch defence minister, there is a reference to the number which was 35.632 refugees from Srebrenica, but there is the word "approximately." This figure is -- may be correct or may be not. What is your opinion? Are you in agreement with the content of this document? Do you agree with this figure or not? Remind me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you were listening carefully a minute ago when I explained what "approximately" means in mathematics, now I remember and I can tell you that maybe in the theory of probability in mathematics or the theory of limit values marked with the word "limes," an exact solution cannot be computed and you cannot put an equation mark before that, which means that the result is completely accurate. Instead of an equation mark, one puts a symbol, which I explained to you is interpreted in mathematics "approximately" or "equal," which means that the deviation is very, very small. In addition to that, I would like to remind you that the government in Sarajevo, with the assistance of the World Health Organization, came at this same figure after counting the refugees on the 4th of August, 1995. So when I took into account the fact that that was done by the Government of Sarajevo, that this was including in the official debriefing report, and that finally it was confirmed by Mr. Jonathan Rooper in his article, means that I had three sources of information that speak about an exactly the same number, and for that reason I took it to be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe. Oh, it's ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, on the basis of your explanation the Chamber has reconsidered its position, especially taking into account that there was no objection by the Defence, the document will be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 7604 shall be assigned Exhibit P2873. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You mentioned yesterday this article called "Srebrenica Icon," and you mentioned that this was a publication or an article in this "Defense & Foreign Affairs" strategic policy magazine; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that the article was published in the magazine entitled "Defense & Foreign Affairs."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to show you 65 ter 7608.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll move to add this document. The witness referred to it yesterday. I believe it is the article that he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, again I take it that you don't object to add this article to the 65 ter exhibit list; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are right, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Leave is granted to add it to the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm afraid I do not have a B/C/S translation of this article, but I'll read to you the title of it just for a moment. On page 1, at the very top, it reads: "Psychological strategy and terrorism, a staff report." And then it says: "The Srebrenica icon. How a Trojan horse for Islamist terrorism was built with western help in the heart of Europe." Do you recognise that title, Mr. Skrbic?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is this the article that you were referring to in your testimony yesterday and just a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could be able -- I would be able to tell you that with full certainly only if I had a translation in Serbian. I believe so, but in order for me to be absolutely certain and to be able to confirm what you're asking me, I would have to have the article in Serbian as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] All right. If we could just go -- Sorry. If we could just go to the bottom of the article. Or just the bottom of the page, sorry. If we could just blow up the very -- the footer. Here you can see that it begins on page 4, that's on the left, it says: "Defense & Foreign Affairs Strategic Policy 9," which is the volume number, and "2003," which is the year. Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that the article? Does that refresh your recollection or help you identify this article as the one you reviewed and were speaking about yesterday and a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that confuses me, sir, is the black square. The translation that was published in the bulletin of the General Staff of Yugoslavia doesn't feature this square. This is what confuses me and this is why I may appear a bit mistrustful, although I recognise everything you are showing me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I can read to you the part in the black square, if that would help you, but I think we probably have identified it sufficiently. It black square it his says: "Bosnia's Islamist leaders are tied directly to 9-11." Then it says: "Balkan-based Iranian and al-Qaeda assets are gearing for major new terror operations to break out of the US 'war on terror,' with concern for the 2004 Athens Olympics." And the third entry says: "The new 'Srebrenica Monument' has been raised as a means of staving off concerns about the Islamist as a terrorist threat."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now if we could just zoom out a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Under point 1 we see that it talks about Bosnia's link to 9-11. It's on the right-hand side of the page. And it talks about the Trojan horse on the left-hand side of the page. And it says: "It came into effect on September 20th, 2003. It was the monument built in Srebrenica to ostensibly commemorate the Muslim victims of Serb 'genocide' in 1995. The monument is a pointed representation solely of the claims disputed by studies of the French and Dutch governments and NATO as well as other sources --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: "... of the radical Islamists of Alija Izetbegovic's Radical Islamist Party of Democratic Action (SDA)." Does that sound familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. This was more or less what I read in the translation of this article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have a request for Mr. Vanderpuye. When reading from the article, could he please slow down, because a lot of the things that he read out went uninterpreted or the interpretation was lagging considerably behind. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is exactly the reason why I asked Mr. Vanderpuye to slow down. And the transcript has to be reviewed at a later stage. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we go to page 3 of this document, on the right hand column we see point number 2, which says "the Srebrenica gambit." If we can blow that up a little bit. That's helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In this part of the document, it says in the first paragraph that: "On the eve of the dedication of a monument to Muslims killed at Srebrenica in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1995, a group which included a former UN official, intelligence experts, and journalists released a statement on September 18, 2003, challenging the alleged casualty number of 7.000 victims as 'vastly inflated and unsupported by evidence.' "They asserted that one-sided interventionist policies permitted al-Qaeda forces and radical Islamists backed by the Iranian clerical government to take root during the Bosnian war, clouding the future of the region."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Slow down, please. We are missing something in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: "As well, they agreed that the memorialization of false numbers in the monument [Realtime transcript read in error "municipal unit"] actually appeared to be intended to perpetuate regional ethnic hatred and distrust and to deliberately punish one of the victim groups in the Bosnian civil war." You read this as well, Mr. Skrbic?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, indeed. However, you may have noticed in my report I did not analyse this article. The only thing I did, I used the figure of 35.000 as my calculation basis. As for the rest of the article, I was really not interested in any of that. The only thing that I had was my own personal curiosity, but that didn't go into my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You can see at the bottom of this page a reference to former BBC journalist - it's the last complete paragraph; that's right - former BBC journalist Jonathan Rooper. That's the same journalist that you referred to during your testimony; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, yes. Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we go to the far right column again. In the second paragraph of this column, you'll see a reference to a Yossef Bodansky. And it says: "Yossef Bodansky, who has written several books on the war in Yugoslavia and also serves as research director of ISSA --" By the way, do you know what ISSA is?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I believe that this has to do with the research of some events or social research. If I had the translation of the abbreviation, I would be able to explain what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How about: International Strategic Studies Association. Does that sound about right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That does sound familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He calls the 7.000 figure "disinformation" and notes that "All independent forensic evidence points to Muslim casualties in the hundreds." That's basically your conclusion, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm glad that you're reading this. I'm glad that the Trial Chamber has an opportunity to see that this fits with my own research.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: To continue on in this paragraph, it says: "Continued emphasis on such allegedly high numbers of Muslim deaths at Srebrenica also obfuscates the Muslim murders in that city earlier of Serb civilians. "Bodansky also wrote extensively on the link between Osama bin Laden and the Bosnian Islamists in numerous articles and special reports and three books," and then they are named. At the bottom of this page, we'll see a reference to Rooper again. And he says -- or, rather, it says in the article: "Rooper points out that the figure of 40.000 inhabitants which the UN used in July 1995, before the capture of Srebrenica, roughly matches the number of former residents accounted for in the aftermath." That's what you conclude, too, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. However, I would like to emphasize that their destiny is known, which means that they were registered somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: "A commander of the Muslim-dominated Army of BH later," if we go to the next page, "confirmed to parliament, in Sarajevo, that 5.000 BH troops escaped largely intact to Tuzla while the UN registered some 35.632 civilian survivors." That's what you were referring to; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I also made calculations based on the figure of 5.000 as well as the figure of 3.000 presented by the ICRC. I made my calculations based on both figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we go to the next paragraph -- or, rather, the one following, it says: "Instead of acknowledging that there was no support for the original figures, Rooper says various means were used to prop up the official story." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did my analysis and I arrived at results which demonstrates that the number of those who were executed can certainly not be expressed in the thousands. And for some dozen years the media and the general public have persevered on something that is a figure of 7.000 or over 7.000 people. That figure may be convincing only if it is supported by propaganda.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you believe that that figure of 7.000 or more than 7.000 people killed, most of whom were summarily executed, is propaganda? Is that right, Mr. Skrbic?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. Please listen carefully to my words. I did not say that the figure of 7.000 is a product of propaganda. I said that it was sold to the general public with the help of propaganda so as to look convincing. I said that I analysed the population of Srebrenica before and after Krivaja 95 operation and I established that there is no difference after the operation that would point to the fact that 7.000 or more than 7.000 militarily able-bodied men were missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Skrbic, we're at an impasse. You say that based on your calculations the number of people that could be potentially victims was something like 397; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's according to one source. According to another source, there is a different figure. There is a third figure and a fourth figure. However, none of these figures are bigger than a thousand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you please give us the other numbers you have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can do that, but I would have to have my report on the screen, and then I'll be able to give you the figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I can put that up in a moment, if you would like, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I can't remember the exhibit number, but I do remember the 65 ter number: 1D01114.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I can give you the report number. I think it's 1-- no, it's D368 --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document, though, while we have it on the screen. And we can come back to it as well, but I think before we switch them I'd like to -- I'd like to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have heard that this was also published in Serbian, in a Serbian gazette. Is this version available?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I might be able to track it down, but I wasn't able to track it down yesterday, and that's why this one is only in English. I suppose we can mark it for identification until I can either track down the other one or have this one translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That would be very helpful, especially for the Defence, to know the text in B/C/S. This document will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 7608 shall be assigned Exhibit P2874 marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, we have your report in e-court now. For my purposes, we can go to page 19, which would be page 22 and 23 in the B/C/S, or in Serbian. And I think that's right. The figure of 397 I'm focussing on you'll find at the bottom of the last paragraph in the English, where it says: "The remainder of 397 men fit for military service might be those who died." On the following page in the English, beginning in the sentence -- it probably should be a paragraph, but the sentence that says: "Since the exact number of Muslim losses during the breakout in the fighting for Srebrenica and in the internecine clashes during that fighting is not known, it is impossible to reliably determine the manner of death of these 397 possible victims." Now, you have indicated that you have other numbers based upon the results of calculating different estimates of various populations; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And those numbers range from what to what?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They range from 118 to 800-something. I can't tell you off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps you can look through your report again during the break and give us after the break the page number where we can find these other numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Based on your calculations of the numbers that you relied on in your report you concluded that the minimum number of people that could have been the victims of the fighting or executed in relation to Srebrenica could have been as low as 118 people?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the lowest figure I arrived at, taking into account various sources of information and using various calculation methodologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And General Tolimir agreed with that? He agrees with that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, maybe Mr. Vanderpuye should give us a reference. I never discussed this issue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. You may remember at the beginning of my examination of this witness I asked him whether or not General Tolimir agreed with his conclusions. If I can find it in the transcript, I'll let you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You recall that, don't you, Mr. Skrbic?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you said, "most probably," or something to that effect; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember my answer. However, I did not have any contacts with the general, so I'm in no position to tell you what he thinks or what his position is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You gave us an explanation about the terms of your engagement, where you said that you would only write the report -- or, rather, that only if they agreed with your report that you would continue with it; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I told them that I wanted to work independently. And I gave them the framework of the topics that I would deal with and the methodology that I would use. I didn't want anybody interfering with that. The only person I spoke to was Mr. Gajic. Unfortunately, I never talked to Mr. Tolimir. Perhaps I should have talked to him as well about all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At page 19019 of the transcript, I asked you: "What I'd like to know ... off the bat is: You presented your report to General Tolimir; is that right? "A. That's right. Through his legal advisor. "Q. Okay. And he agrees with the conclusions that you draw in your report? "A. Well, I think that since he accepted me as a witness here, I believe that he agrees with my conclusions." So my question to you is: I'm asking you about one of your conclusions - does he agree with it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, do I have to repeat what I said? If he agreed that I should come here, this implies that he accepted or agreed with my conclusions, the one that I presented in my expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. And I said to you just a moment before we got into this discussion we were at an impasse because your conclusions account for, at most, a few hundred victims of the Srebrenica events; whereas the evidence presented in this case establishes several thousand. Is it your position that the difference in those numbers is a fabrication of the evidence in this case?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have a position about the evidence you refer to, about whether they -- about whether that evidence has been fabricated or not. If you've been listening to me carefully, and I have to repeat this, I said that I started investigating the matter to determine whether what you are claiming is, in fact, true or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And as the analysis has demonstrated, the claims that you are making are not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I referred you to 7608. Okay. The document that was -- the article, "Srebrenica Icon," I want to ask you about another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 7602 in e-court, please. This is a document, Mr. President, that I ask leave to add to the 65 ter list of the Prosecution. It is a publication relating to these matters by Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it from the previous answer of Mr. Tolimir that he doesn't object, and therefore leave is granted to add it to the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Skrbic?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a book that I wrote, the title of which is: "Srebrenica - Genocide Perpetrated Against the Truth."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you pick that title yourself?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when was it published?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was published in March of last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: March 2011 is when it was published?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When did you complete it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was more than a year before it was published.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So sometime in 2010 or maybe even 2009; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Because I was competing -- I was in competition to public this book within the Government of Republika Srpska. The ministry of culture has a competition every year for the publication of new books. This took about a year. It took me about a year for me to receive the response -- to receive their response. I didn't win the competition, and then I tried to find other means of having this book published.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The title, "Genocide of the Truth" or "of Truth," what is that intended to mean?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that the truth is the first casualty of war, and then everything else follows. As far as I can remember, a famous Greek philosopher used these words. In the forward, Dr. Mirceta Vemic mentioned the name of that philosopher. He is the person who draft the forward of the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, a minute ago when I asked you -- well, maybe more than a minute ago, but a little while ago when I asked you about this document you referred to, "The Srebrenica Icon" that we read -- I read from extensively, you said that you found the number in the document, in that article, and that's what you used, but basically you weren't interested in it; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I really haven't understood your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the reference be provided to the witness rather than paraphrasing what was said for the benefit of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At page 13, line 4 through 13, my question was - and I read out part of this article: "As well they agreed that the memorialization of false numbers," it says in the transcript "in the municipal unit," "actually appeared to be intended to perpetuate regional ethnic hatred and distrust and to deliberately punish one of the groups," it says "grouped" in the transcript, "in the Bosnia civil war. "You read this as well, Mr. Skrbic?" was my question. Your answer was: "I did, indeed. However, you may have noticed in my report I did not analyse this article. The only thing I did, I used the figure of 35.000 as my calculation basis. As for the rest of the article, I was really not interested in any of that." Does that refresh your recollection as to what you did in relation to that article?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you weren't interested in any of that article; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean when you ask me whether I was interested in it or not. If I hadn't been interested in it, I wouldn't have read it at all. But I didn't use it for the purposes of a political or security analysis in relation to terrorism, for example, or in relation to any other matter. All I did was use the information I found in that article and I used that information to make the calculations I made in my expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let me go to page 12 in e-court of the book in English, and I believe page 18 in the Serbian. I am going to refer you in the Serbian to the paragraph that begins under the bolded text at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And just a moment in the English, because I seem to have a different version. Okay. There's another translation in e-court. It should be ERN 6810391. If we go to the bottom of the page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I want to refer -- well, I've already referred you to the text. In this document we can see here it says: "'Second, by 1998, thousands of bodies excavated from all across Bosnia were stored at the Tuzla airport. Despite state-of-the-art DNA testing, only 200 bodies have been linked to Srebrenica.'" This quote from the article entitled "The Srebrenica Icon" published in "Defense & Foreign Affairs" strategic policy issue number 9, 2003, pages 4 through 8, the translation of which was published in the information bulletin of translations issue 2/2004, Centre for Documentation and Information in Military Science, Belgrade, it says "Balkanska 53." "This was a powerful incentive factor for me to tackle the issue of Srebrenica victims in more detail." Those are your words; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your book that we have in front of us now is nearly identical in every respect to your expert report that you produced for General Tolimir in 2011; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are almost right. But in the report there is something that isn't contained in the book and that is the first part that refers to the number of captured individuals who were transported and to the number of men fit for military service who were killed, members of the 28th Division in this particular case. As for the other information, on the whole that information is the same as the information in my book.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It contains all the same information, with the exception of the first few pages of your report, on the population of Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. But there are perhaps certain amendments in other parts, too, but one could say that that part of the book did serve as the groundwork for this expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, when you say "groundwork," in fact, it incorporates all of the identical figures, tables, and diagrams, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct in relation to the ones that were, in fact, taken from the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it advances the same arguments.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same arguments are put forward and the conclusion is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You gave, in your book, several reasons why you wrote it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could go to page 12 in the English and page 17 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You say first -- well, before that: "Why did I choose to commit to truth and research it? There are several reasons for this. I shall state -- I shall only state those which are most important. "First, simply, I doubted the possibility that any of my colleagues, professional officers and non-commissioned officers, could line up several hundred or several thousand enemy soldiers and civilians and order that they be executed or take part in this misdeed." That's one of your motivations for producing this book; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I really had such doubts. But as you can see, I didn't say that that was not correct. I just had my doubts and then I wanted to determine what the real situation actually was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Second: "By 1998 thousands of bodies excavated from all across Bosnia were stored at the Tuzla airport," as we discussed previously. And you say: "'Despite state-of the-art DNA testing, only 200 bodies have been link to Srebrenica.'" Quoting this article we spoke about; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And I have to admit once more that this was a significant reason for which I got involved in this, but it was a personal reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, certainly you knew by the time you wrote this book in late -- either late 2009 or in 2010 that through DNA testing probably more than 5.000 bodies had been linked to Srebrenica at that time. You were part of the Miletic Defence, and certainly you would have known that; isn't that right, Mr. Skrbic?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have that information when I wrote the book. I didn't have that information on the DNA findings. I had no information apart from the information I had used in this article, and I used this information as a sort of additional motivating factor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, it wouldn't have been too hard to find out: by making a simple phone call to the Miletic Defence to find out what the state of the DNA identification evidence had been at that time; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I had asked for them, I believe I would have been able to obtain that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the very bottom of this page, the last sentence, you talk about your conclusion, and you say: "Based on this fact, it can be concluded that following the end of Operation Krivaja 95 --" thank you, "the entire or almost the entire population of Srebrenica left for Tuzla and the surrounding area in various ways and were registered among the refugees from Srebrenica on 4 August 1995, alive," in bold. Yes?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we go to page 14 in the English, page 21 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I want to direct your attention to the following. You say under number 4: "My internal rebellion and instinct, as well as my internal resistance in dissatisfaction with almost daily perennial media bombardment with the alleged facts that the VRS and its members, supported by Serbian forces, committed an alleged genocide against the Srebrenica Muslims without anyone proving it, but where at the same time it was to be conditionally accepted as truth, kept adding fuel and strengthening my will to research the Muslim losses in Srebrenica during and after Operation Krivaja 95 and find out whether the official version of these losses is consistent with the truth or not? Something you've repeated to some extent today. Right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What do you by "without anybody proving it"?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that must be clear. Nobody proved that 7- or 8.000 or more than 7.000 Muslim men fit for military service had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You say: "'The imposing of truth,' about the official version of Muslim losses, however, is not encouraged by the daily perennial media bombardment by facts on the alleged genocide against Srebrenica Muslims. An equally efficient means is the fact that the media are ignoring facts about the events in and around Srebrenica from other sources, which the author of this book was able to experience personally." You go on to say that when you reached "the first tangible data and results proving that the Muslim victims from Srebrenica cannot be expressed in thousands and that all or almost all Muslims left Srebrenica in various ways during and after Operation Krivaja 95 for Tuzla and its surrounding where they were registered as refugees from Srebrenica, alive," in bold, "I immediately offered these results to leading electronic and printed media in Serbia, news agencies, and some political parties, including those in power, expecting them to publish this data without asking for anything in return. As I said, the findings and the results I reached in this research of the events in and around Srebrenica were absolutely ignored by the media." This is one of the reasons why you undertook the research was to prove a point; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not one of the main reasons for which I undertook the research. When I said that, all I wanted to say is that some other findings about the events in Srebrenica reached the public with a lot of difficulty. In relation to the findings that became the official version, the official version was that 8.000 Muslim men fit for military service had been executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, it's clear from your book, in this particular passage, that your research was rejected on more than one occasion and by more than one entity; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one rejected my research. They simply refused to publish it in the media, in printed form or in electronic form. However, in one newspaper my -- an article on my book was published in two parts. However, after the second part was published by a -- that newspaper, the newspaper ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You offered your research to political parties. What parties were those?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to almost all important parties. And when I say that, I mean the parties that had members of parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Why would you offer your research to a political party in the first place?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because it's a matter of public research, and my research didn't tally with the official version. It was to show that there were -- there was other information on the number of men fit for military service who had been executed. I believed that this was information that was relevant in a state that is led by parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: On the following page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Mindua has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Prosecutor, I apologise. I just have a minor question for the witness. In transcript page 29, line 11, you said that after the publication of the second part of your article the newspaper ceased to exist, was no longer published. What do you mean? Since that point in time this newspaper is no longer being published, what was the reason for that, if that was the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, but that was really the case. That's what happened. The title of the newspaper is "Grom," "Thunder." I don't know why it ceased to exist. I don't know whether it was a simple coincidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What kind of newspaper was it - a daily newspaper? Had it been in existence for several years? Was it a reputable newspaper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, it was a weekly publication that was published in a "kurir," a daily newspaper, and it wasn't particularly important in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I think we need the first break now, and you may continue after the break. I would kindly ask the witness to look into your report during the break and to give us the reference to the possible numbers of victims. Thank you. We resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, I noticed before the break that one comment you made in answering a question of Judge Mindua was not acceptable, when you said: "If you would have listened to me more careful," something to that effect. This is not an acceptable answer to a question put to you in this courtroom. I asked you to look into your report to provide us with the numbers of possible victims. Can you give us the reference to your report, please, and give us the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I really and most sincerely apologise for making this slip of the tongue. Now I'm going to give you the page numbers in my report where the references of possible losses can be found, and, if necessary, I can provide explanation why each and every one of these references were taken and what they indicate. First, page 26 in Serbian, last paragraph. It reads: "The lower limit of the results of this calculation (13.903) which is --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I have to interrupt you. I would be glad if we can have that page on the screen in B/C/S, and you said it's page 26. We need the respective page in English, too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can see, that's page 23 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue with your answer. I'm not interested in an explanation. I would like to have the four figures. One you have mentioned before the break, that was 397. The other was 118. And which are the other two figures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the last paragraph you can see two numbers: 1.097 or 188. Now, I have to explain why I put the word "or." I did that because if I make my calculations based on the information about members of the 28th Division who managed to break through but were not registered among the 35.632, according to the ICRC reports there were 3.000 such troops. And this number, 1.097, corresponds to the number that served to calculate the final figure of 3.000. Number 188 is the result of the calculation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, before the break you said there are four possible numbers of losses. Can you give me the four numbers from your report, the four different numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's one. Then on page 29, at the end of the first paragraph, we have figures 213 or 1.291. On that same page, in the bold section of the text, we had the figure of 897. And then on page 31, line 16 and 7 [as interpreted], we have the figure of 618. And in the last paragraph on that same page, we have number 118. All these figures indicate that there is a negative difference or a shortcoming of able-bodied men after Krivaja 95 operation if compared to the figures that existed before the operation. Naturally, for each of these numbers I can give you additional explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you for four numbers. Nothing else. I just want to have the numbers you were referring to on page 16 of today's transcript. And I refer you to that again. I don't want to be confused. Mr. Vanderpuye asked you about the number of 397, potential victims, and your answer was: "That's according to one source. According to another source, there is a different figure. There is a third figure and a fourth figure. However, none of these figures are bigger than a thousand." Please, what do you mean by "these four figures"? I would like to have these four figures. And without any explanation. Just the numbers, please. In your last answer you gave more figures. Which are the four figures you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, those four figures are among this larger number of figures that I have just cited. So that means that there are more than four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I give it up. Mr. Skrbic, another question. We see, or we saw, on the screen your book you have recently published. You said it is -- the content is quite identical to the report you have prepared for this trial. Earlier today I asked you about any publications you have made, and you said you have given a report to a conference in Moscow and that paper was published. Is that identical with the book we have discussed, or is it a different paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After publishing the paper and after I delivered it at the Russian Academy of Sciences, I continued my work, and this initial paper served as a basis for me to expand my research. And as a result of such an expanded research, I arrived at the book in its present form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At page 3, lines 1 through 5, you said: "I published only one paper in the proceedings," and there are some mistakes in the transcript, "for the Russian Academy of Science, and my scientific work was entitled: 'The Analysis of the Srebrenica Population.' That was a paper delivered at the international conference held in Moscow in April 2009." You said you published one paper. Is this the book, or is it a different paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's much shorter than the book. This paper has about 30 pages, whereas the book has many, many more pages. But the information contained in the paper coincide to part of the information in the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Why did you say, "I published only one paper"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because that's how I understood your question. You asked me if I published any scientific works anywhere, and that's why I responded that I did and that that paper of mine was scientifically verified. If that were not the case, it would not have been published in the proceedings from that conference, and that is why I mentioned only that paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I didn't use the word "scientific." I was specifically referring to any kind of publications. And then I said, "Did you publish anything?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really understood your question in the way that I have just explained to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think we were on page 14 in the English, and I think probably page 22 in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, the question of what happened to the population of Srebrenica following its collapse in July 1995 is something you've been researching for a number of years; fair to say?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's something that you've researched and given talks on and is the subject of your book which you completed back in either late 2009 or 2010; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what you mean by "given talks"?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, have you presented your paper anywhere, or the thesis that's contained in your paper?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I understand. Yes. And I already confirmed that, that I presented my paper on the analysis of the movement of the population of Srebrenica at the Russian Academy of Sciences.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And so your thesis is essentially this: That based on looking at the population in Srebrenica - say of about 40.000 - around July 1995, and looking at the population of registered refugees, of 35.632 plus however other many men you say arrived from the column, that that leaves some few hundred people that could be potential victims of the crimes in Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what the results of this analysis show.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, that's what you believe, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason to doubt it, because I used the information that came from relevant sources. And not a single piece of information was made up by me. Each and every bit of information that I use for my calculations can be found in a relevant document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And you came to those conclusions without making up any information, but also without looking at information - documentary evidence in this case and other cases - concerning the number of missing and dead from Srebrenica following its collapse; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. At the beginning of this trial I said that I opted to apply a research methodology that involves following the movement of Muslim survivors in Srebrenica prior and after Krivaja 95 operation because I had quite sufficient information about the number of the inhabitants before and after the operation. In addition to that, I can say that I did not have any particular need to delve into other researches that applied different methodologies. I opted for this particular methodology.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When I first started asking you questions on cross-examination, I asked you about the documents you received or reviewed in relation to the preparation of your report. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I asked you if you asked the Defence for any particular documents. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. And I responded that I didn't ask for any documentation because I thought it was their duty to provide me with the documents in order to enable me to perform my task for the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you reach your conclusions in your paper -- I'm sorry, in your expert report, and your book - and I suppose your paper, frankly - without having reviewed any exhumation reports, any pathology reports, any autopsy reports; right? No forensic evidence related to this case.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't do that because I don't know almost anything about forensics.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You didn't ask for any documents concerning the number of missing, for example; right? You mentioned the ICRC reports. Did you consider the number of missing in the ICRC lists in terms of determining the population data that you reported in your expert paper?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did mention the findings and the lists of the ICRC on the missing persons, but that would actually go beyond the scope of my methodology, and for that reason I didn't study the lists of the missing persons but I did become acquainted with them in the course of preparing my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In the list that you reviewed, how many missing persons related to Srebrenica was reported by the ICRC at the time that you reviewed it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember at the moment the exact number. But there is plenty of information, different information, about the missing persons in the lists of the ICRC, of the NGO called Medecins Sans Frontieres, and other international humanitarian organisations. But the first two lists, the one of the ICRC and the Medecins Sans Frontieres, were the ones that I saw most often.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand that. My question was: How many people were reported missing in the reports that you reviewed? If you can't remember, you can tell us that too.

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, between 8.000 and 10.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that's not in your report, is it? Either that you reviewed that documentation or that the number reported in that documentation was 8- to 10.000 or 8- or 10.000 missing people?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A while ago I told you that I decided to apply the methodology of following the survivors, and my entire focus was on that methodology. I admitted, honestly, that I didn't need to go into other lists, that I didn't think that I should devote any particular attention to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We talked a minute ago -- a minute ago - more than a minute ago about DNA evidence. Did you review any reports relating to DNA-identified missing people related to the fall of Srebrenica in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just came across this piece of information at a glance.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the information you came across, how many DNA-identified missing people from Srebrenica was reported in that?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact data because the documents that I reviewed were drafted in different years and they contain different information, and for that reason I cannot say that I remember. There are significant differences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said you don't remember the exact data. In your recollection, approximately how many have been reported?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you asking me about the number of exhumed and identified persons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm exactly referring to the question Mr. Vanderpuye put to you: How many DNA-identified missing people from Srebrenica were reported in that report? To your recollection, how many, roughly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can tell you now that I just remembered a document that I did not include in my report because it went beyond my methodology, but I did read it. It was a document from the year 2007 in which an authorised official from Sarajevo is sending this document in which it is said that up to 2007 around 4.400 individuals were identified, and this figure relates to people from ten various municipalities, not only Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I asked you at the very beginning of your cross-examination what documents you were provided with and whether you asked for any, and in your answer you said you "asked to be supplied and provided with all the documents that he," Mr. Gajic or Mr. Tolimir, "can offer that might be useful and which could fit with the idea of the report, as I explained it to Mr. Gajic." You remember giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the reference of the Trial Chamber, that's at page 19021, lines 17 through 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you remember that Mr. Skrbic?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember. And I repeat: I didn't ask for any special documents. Not a single one. I asked them to provide me with those documents that might be of use to me in drafting my expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you explained, at lines 23 through the next page, line 1, that you explained to Mr. Gajic that based on the documents, your "desire was to confirm or demonstrate whether it was accurate, the information that more than 7.000 able-bodied men were killed." As we state it, summarily executed. "That's as far as the ... report is concerned." That's what the purpose of your report was, and you asked for documents relevant to that end; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, all the documents that could be of some use and that could have supported my methodology is what I asked for. I didn't ask for anything else on top of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me show you 65 ter -- I'm sorry, P1776. I'll wait a moment for the Serbian to be uploaded. This is a document - you can see in the title - it's called a "2009 Integrated Report on Srebrenica Missing, Including a Progress Report on DNA-Based Identification." Have you ever seen this before, Mr. Skrbic?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've not seen this document. However, I saw other documents drafted by Brunborg, those that were drafted before 2009. I've not seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was this provided -- were those documents, rather, provided to you by General Tolimir's Defence or General Miletic's Defence, the ones that you saw?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody did. I received a huge number of documents, perhaps over 2500 folders. I really don't know who provided me with what. I can't remember. In any case, it was one of those two Defence teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could go to page 6 of this document. I think its the same in both the Serbian and the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At paragraph 2.1, table 1, you can see a graphic representation of the overall number of missing persons related to the fall of Srebrenica, and it says: "7.692." Is that a number you've seen before or have heard about?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you consider that this report would have been relevant to your review of the number of individuals that might have been the victims of crimes related to the fall of Srebrenica in 1995?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I repeat: I opted for the methodology which followed the movement of surviving Muslims. I didn't do anything else. I did not use any other methodology. It was never my intention. My main purpose was to follow the movement of Muslim survivors, i.e., people who lived there before the operation and who survived after the operation. The purpose of that exercise was to establish whether there was a negative difference in the population number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In order to determine the population number, don't you have to consider not just the living people but the missing people, too?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the difference in the number of survivors I determined the number of those who had gone missing or who had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I understand what you're saying, are you suggesting that the 7.692 individuals that is indicated in this document is only correct to the extent that your report arrives at a conclusion that only 118 or maybe 618 may actually be missing or dead? In other words, do you reject this conclusion as to the number of missing people as a part of the population of Srebrenica in 1995?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you've already heard and as you have seen in my expert report, I'm not saying anything, I'm not claiming anything; I'm just providing the results of my analysis. I arrived at only one conclusion, and we can agree that this is my claim and that is that the results of my analysis show that the losses of able-bodied Muslims cannot be expressed in the thousands.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I have your answer. Let me show you P170. Mr. Skrbic, have you seen this document before? It's entitled: "Update to the Summary of Forensic Evidence - Exhumation of the Graves and Surface Remains Recoveries Related to Srebrenica and Zepa - April 2010," by Investigator Dusan Janc, dated 21 April 2010. Any of that seem familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've not seen this report before. All the forensic reports that I had an occasion to see, I simply skipped all of them because I don't know anything about forensic science. I'm not competent to either look at these reports to interpret their contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, let me show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At page 5 in the English and page 6 in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'm showing you is the totals, total figures, of identified individuals by DNA analysis recovered from over a hundred sites. In the interest of saving time, I won't show you the other ones that precede this, but there you have it. And you can see here in -- for Srebrenica and Zepa graves, it says, total: 5.777, as of 2010. That there are surface remains of identified individuals by DNA analysis of 703. You may not be aware of this, but these were mostly recovered in the area of the route taken by the column towards the free territory from Srebrenica. In addition, you will see 76 identified DNA remains recovered from other areas. And the total number of Srebrenica- and Zepa-related victims identified by DNA - at that point - was 6.556. Now, those are just numbers. Did you consider? Obviously you hadn't seen this report, but did you ask for this kind of information from General Tolimir or Mr. Gajic, rather, the Tolimir Defence?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask for any such document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And they didn't give it to you either; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that I have not seen this one before. This is the first time I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were you made aware -- well, first of all, have you heard of the International Commission for Missing Persons? Have you heard that name before?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you aware that the director of forensic sciences for that organisation testified in this case? And during the course of his testimony --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the Court's benefit, that was on the 25th of February, 2011.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- he testified that that organisation, which engages in DNA testing, identified -- or, rather, issued 6.441 match reports related to Srebrenica. And that was as of February 2011. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that the gentleman that you have just mentioned testified before this Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now that you've seen some of the evidence in this case relating to the number of victims following the fall of Srebrenica and Zepa, would you change anything in your report with respect to your conclusions as to the number of potential victims there might have been?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say anything about that. Having thrown a perfunctory look on the page before me, I have tried to find the period for which the victims were reported. Is it for July/August 1995 or the entire war in Bosnia-Herzegovina? I -- what I have noticed is the fact that these victims were not the result of the events in July and August 1995. In order to be able to say something, first of all I would have to familiarise myself with the basics of forensic. I have already told you I don't know anything about forensic science. I am a military expert, and my field of expertise is command, control, and management of the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Would you have liked to have seen this kind of material before you drafted your report? Would you have liked to have had an opportunity to analyse it or at least take a look at it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I would love to look at all the existing documents; however, it wouldn't mean much to me if I didn't understand the area of expertise that such reports cover.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: I just want to scroll down for me to see the top of this page displayed on e-court. What -- maybe it's a clarification for Mr. Vanderpuye, what is the -- starting from the left, the third column, what does that denote?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The dates?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Those are the dates of the exhumations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay, thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, you concede, don't you, that thousands of Muslim prisoners were taken into the custody of VRS forces following the collapse of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've come across this information. This is exactly what it says in the documents, thousands.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you have some indication as to what happened to those thousands of prisoners that came into the custody of the VRS following the collapse of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only indication that I had was the information that I found in a document. I can't remember which one at this moment. But I know that the commander of the Zvornik Brigade opened the corridor without consulting anybody. He did it of his own accord to allow those people to go through.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Maybe we misunderstood each other, but when I said "custody," I mean custody. They were detained by the VRS. Arrested, captured, and detained. Do you concede that?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I concede to that. You say that people were taken in custody in Bratunac and then transferred to the territory of the 1st Zvornik Brigade and later executed, according to you. This is the information that I used in my calculations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So let me see if I can sort this out: Am I to infer from your calculations that you included the thousands of prisoners that were in VRS custody as among those that arrived safely in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I did not treat them separately. The results of my analysis show that able-bodied males from Srebrenica left and arrived in Tuzla and its environs. They arrived there. They were registered. And their number could not have been more than a thousand.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me show you P125. This is a document the Trial Chamber has seen. Have you seen it before? It's a document that was sent from the forward command post of the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment. It says, "Borike, 1400 hours." And it refers to the procedure for treatment of prisoners of war. Have you seen this before?

utterances.speaker: RATKO SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It says, in the first line, there are over 1.000 members of the former 28th Division of the so-called BH army captured in the area of Dusanovo (Kasaba). Prisoners are under control of the military police battalion of the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment. Yes?
